History and Physical (H&P – Detailed)

Consult Summary:
25-year-old woman with a 2-month history of escalating work-related anxiety, insomnia, morning palpitations, and low mood; counselled on talking therapies and basic blood tests arranged.

History:
• Presenting complaint: Progressive anxiety for ≈2 months, worst on work-days.  
• Onset/trigger: Began soon after starting a new, highly stressful head-office role in fashion retail; boss perceived as hostile.  
• Course: Gradually worsening; daily dread of leaving the house; no previous similar episode.  
• Sleep: Goes to bed 22:00–23:00, falls asleep “after hours,” total sleep ≈3–4 h; shallow; wakes before alarm with racing heart.  
• Palpitations: Irregular rapid heartbeat on waking, lasting 2–10 min; associated fear of heart attack; mild chest discomfort but no frank chest pain.  
• Daytime effects: Marked fatigue, low energy, anhedonia, avoidance of friends/hobbies (running, tennis). Still attends work but contemplates calling in sick most mornings.  
• Mood: Feels “down/unhappy” most days, including weekends; denies suicidal ideation or self-harm.  
• Other systems: No weight loss, tremor, gastrointestinal change, or previous panic attacks.  
• Pertinent negatives: No prior psychiatric history; no drug use; no true chest pain or syncope.

Past Medical History:
• None reported.

Medications:
• None currently used (no prescriptions or over-the-counter agents mentioned).  
Allergies: Not documented.

Social History:
• Lives with parents in South Wimbledon.  
• Occupation: Head-office employee, fashion retailer.  
• Alcohol: Binges most Fridays/Saturdays (“quite a lot,” exceeds limits) + occasional weekday wine.  
• Tobacco: Occasional smoker.  
• Recreational drugs: Denied.

Family History:
• Mother with history of depression.

Physical Examination:
• Vitals: Not recorded (video consultation).  
• General / Cardiovascular / Mental state: Not formally examined; patient appeared distressed on video per clinician comment.  
• Remainder: Not recorded.

Investigations:
• Plan for “basic blood tests” (unspecified screening; likely FBC, TSH, electrolytes, etc.) to evaluate palpitations and rule out medical contributors.

Assessment & Plan:

Overall Impression:
Probable adjustment disorder with anxiety (early generalised anxiety picture) secondary to new job stress, with associated insomnia and functional impairment; depressive features present but no suicidality. Palpitations likely anxiety-related, awaiting blood-test screen.

DDx Integration (brief):
1. Adjustment disorder / evolving Generalised Anxiety Disorder – temporal link to new job; pervasive worry; somatic tension; functional impact.  
2. Major depressive episode (with anxious distress) – low mood, anhedonia, fatigue; no suicidality.  
3. Hyperthyroidism – palpitations/anxiety; will be screened with bloods. (No weight loss/tremor).

Issue 1: Anxiety disorder (work-related)  
• Education on condition; reassurance.  
• Self-referral link provided for NHS talking therapies (CBT).  
• Online CBT/sleep-hygiene resources sent.  
• Advise return if worsening, inability to cope, or panic attacks develop.  
• Medication (e.g., SSRIs) to be considered only if non-pharmacological measures inadequate.

Issue 2: Insomnia / sleep disturbance  
• Sleep-hygiene advice included in resource pack.  
• Monitor response; escalate if persistent.

Issue 3: Palpitations – likely anxiety-mediated, but rule-out medical causes  
• Arrange basic blood screen (FBC, TFTs, U&E, glucose, ferritin) via support line.  
• GP review 1 week post-tests to discuss results and assess need for further cardiac work-up (e.g., ECG, Holter) if symptoms persist.

Issue 4: Alcohol use  
• Counsel on safe limits; recommend tracking intake and reducing binge pattern.  
• Provide signposting to alcohol-reduction resources if desired.

General plan items:  
• Safety-net advice: seek urgent care for chest pain, syncope, or suicidal thoughts.  
• Documentation of consultation summary in patient record; copy of resources emailed.

Quality checks:
● Missing but expected: Exact current medication list and drug/food allergies not elicited.  
● Conflicts: None between transcript and DDx.  
● Transcript quality: Clear; no notable audio gaps.
